title: Human/Agent CLI Workflow Layer
description:
The repo-review CLI has useful low-level primitives, but humans and agents still
need to manually compose too much of the updated-repo review workflow. The CLI
needs a stable workflow layer that lets a human start, resume, inspect, ingest,
and finish review runs while preserving structured JSON output for agents and
tests.
design:
Keep the existing primitive commands available. Build workflow commands above
them, persist review run records under the reviewed repo, expose state discovery,
make status operational, enrich agent-context from a command schema, and
standardize human output, dry-run behavior, delivery, feedback, and template
access.

The governing design principle is operational-first: prefer workflow summaries
and next safe actions over configuration dumps, and prefer stable workflow nouns
over requiring users to reconstruct primitive command pipelines.

Do not build a formal skill until the high-level CLI workflow commands are
stable. The skill should eventually select workflow commands and summarize
artifacts; it should not encode unstable low-level command choreography.
acceptance_criteria:
- A human can start an updated-repo review with one command.
- A human can resume an incomplete review with one command.
- Review runs have durable ledger entries under `.repo-review/runs.jsonl`.
- The CLI can discover and validate prior review states without manual path
  handoff.
- Human output gives bounded summaries, warnings, artifact paths, and next
  actions.
- `--json` output remains stable and parseable for agents.
- Consequential mutations support `--dry-run`.
- Artifact-producing commands use consistent delivery semantics.
- `agent-context`, help, README snippets, and manifest entries are generated
  from or validated against a richer command schema.
- Feedback and decision templates are operationally discoverable from the CLI.

- Existing JSON-mode success output remains parseable in tests.
- Failure diagnostics remain off parseable stdout.
- Tests cover stdout/stderr separation for representative success and failure

- Tests identify current JSON fields that must remain stable during workflow

title: Add State Discovery Commands

Structured output should include review state ID, repo name, repo root, repo
remote when known, commit when known, mode, creation time when known, claim

The ranking rule for `state latest` can be decided in this issue. It should be
documented and tested so the CLI never silently picks a surprising prior state.

- `state latest` resolves one state or refuses with a clear ambiguity diagnostic.

title: Implement Review Start Delta
description:
A human should be able to start a delta review of an updated repo with one
command. Agents should be able to run the same workflow with stable `--json`
output and no prompts.
design:
Add `repo-review review start --mode delta`. It should discover or validate the
prior review state, generate a bounded diff report, map changed files to claims,
write artifacts into a predictable run directory, package a reviewer-ready
prompt, record a durable run entry, and stop at `prompt_ready` unless blocked or
failed earlier.

The command should advance through all safe internal setup transitions in one
invocation. It should avoid duplicate runs using the natural key `(repo, range,
review_state)` unless `--new-run` is supplied.

- `review start --mode delta` creates or reuses an appropriate run record.
- The command can produce diff, impact, and prompt artifacts in one invocation.
- The resulting run normally reaches `prompt_ready`.
- Duplicate run detection uses repo, range, and review state.
- `--new-run` allows an explicit separate run.
- Human output summarizes repo, range, prior state, output dir, created
  artifacts, surfaced claims, warnings, and next action.
- `--json --no-input` never prompts and returns stable structured fields.
- `--dry-run` reports reads, writes, blocking files, warnings, and next command
  without writing.

title: Implement Review Package And Continue
description:
Review runs need commands to assemble or reassemble reviewer-ready packages and
to tell a human or agent exactly where an incomplete run left off.
design:
Add `repo-review review package` and `repo-review review continue`.

`review package` should create or update the prompt packet and supporting
artifact package for a run, moving `impact_ready` to `prompt_ready` when
successful.

`review continue` should be report-only by default. It should inspect the run
ledger, map the current status to the next concrete action, and print the
command that would advance the run. Mutating behavior requires explicit
`--apply`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `review package` can package a run from `impact_ready` to `prompt_ready`.
- `review package` supports `--dry-run`.
- `review continue --run <id>` and `review continue --latest` resolve runs.
- Report-only `review continue` emits no mutation outcome.
- `review continue --apply` performs only safe deterministic transitions.
- Every run status maps to a concrete next action or blocker explanation.
- Human and JSON output are both covered by tests.

title: Implement Review Ingest And Finish
description:
After a reviewer or model returns output, the workflow layer needs to attach,
validate, ingest, and finish the run without making unresolved human decisions
on the operator's behalf.
design:
Add `repo-review review ingest` and `repo-review review finish`.

`review ingest --attach-only` should attach reviewer output to a run and move
`prompt_ready` to `review_received` without importing claims or drift. Normal
`review ingest` should validate the artifact kind, attach it if needed, delegate
to existing ingest behavior where possible, update run status to `ingested`, and
report candidate claims, drift, and unresolved decisions.

`review finish` should validate that a run is finishable, refuse missing
artifacts or unresolved decisions, record final artifact paths and completion
metadata, and move the run to `complete`. It should record completion, not judge
unresolved review questions.
acceptance_criteria:
- `review ingest --attach-only` records reviewer output and moves the run to
  `review_received`.
- `review ingest` validates artifact kind and updates the run to `ingested`.
- Ingest output reports candidate claims, drift, warnings, and next decisions.
- `review finish` refuses incomplete or unresolved runs.
- `review finish` moves finishable runs to `complete`.
- Both commands support `--dry-run`.
- Both commands emit stable JSON and concise human summaries.

title: Define Run Transition Contracts
description:
Review run statuses need explicit meanings, next actions, and command ownership
so `review continue`, `review status`, and future agents can reason about a run
without guessing which command should run next.
design:
Define the status set `created`, `diff_ready`, `impact_ready`, `prompt_ready`,
`review_received`, `ingested`, `drift_ready`, `complete`, `blocked`, and
`failed`. For each status, record its meaning and next action.

Define transition ownership:
- none -> `created`: `review start`
- `created` -> `diff_ready`: `review start` internal step, or `diff` once run
  binding exists
- `diff_ready` -> `impact_ready`: `review start` internal step, or `impact`
  once run binding exists
- `impact_ready` -> `prompt_ready`: `review start` internal step,
  `review package`, or `export-prompt` once run binding exists
- `prompt_ready` -> `review_received`: `review ingest --attach-only`, or an
  equivalent future attach behavior
- `review_received` -> `ingested`: `review ingest`
- `ingested` -> `drift_ready`: `drift surface` once run binding exists
- `drift_ready` -> `complete`: `review finish`
- any -> `blocked`: any command that reaches a human-decision point or missing
  required input
- any -> `failed`: any command after recording a durable failure and recovery
  hint
acceptance_criteria:
- Status meanings and next actions are represented in code or schema.
- Producing commands for each transition are represented in code or schema.
- `review continue` can derive a next action from every status.
- Tests cover the status-to-next-action mapping.
- `blocked` and `failed` include recovery or decision hints.
notes:

title: Define Mutation Outcome Contracts
description:
Safe retries require mutating commands to distinguish what happened instead of
returning vague success. Each mutating command should advertise the subset of
mutation outcomes it may emit, while read-only commands should emit no mutation
outcome values.
design:
Record allowed mutation outcomes per command in the command schema. Initial
outcomes are `created`, `updated`, `existing`, `imported`, `replaced`,
`unchanged`, and `dry_run`.

Initial ownership:
- `state bootstrap`: `created`, `existing`, `replaced`, `dry_run`
- `claims import`: `created`, `updated`, `existing`, `imported`, `replaced`,
  `unchanged`, `dry_run`
- `review start`: `created`, `existing`, `updated`, `dry_run`
- `review package`: `created`, `existing`, `updated`, `dry_run`
- `review ingest`: `created`, `updated`, `existing`, `imported`, `unchanged`,
  `dry_run`
- `review finish`: `updated`, `unchanged`, `dry_run`
- `runs prune`: `updated`, `unchanged`, `dry_run`

Read-only commands, including `state validate`, `state latest`, `state list`,
`state get`, `runs list`, `runs get`, `review status`, and report-only
`review continue`, should not emit mutation outcome values.
acceptance_criteria:
- The command schema records allowed mutation outcomes per mutating command.
- Read-only commands are marked as non-mutating and do not emit mutation
  outcomes.
- Tests fail if a command emits an outcome outside its allowed set.
- Dry-run outputs use the `dry_run` outcome consistently.
